from.place: proof, diagonal step: a Koszul-regular immersion is perfect

title: A Koszul-regular closed immersion is perfect
statement: Let Y be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let i:Z\to Y be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Assume that every point of Y has an affine open neighbourhood U=\operatorname{Spec}A on which the ideal I\subset A of Z\cap U is generated by a finite Koszul-regular sequence of A [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Then i_*\mathcal O_Z is locally quasi-isomorphic to the bounded Koszul complex [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex] on that sequence, whose terms are finite free modules. Consequently i is a perfect closed immersion [def-sc-perfect-closed-immersion], and i_*\mathcal O_Z is a perfect complex on Y [def-pc-perfect-complex].

source.place: Tag 068C, Lemma 37.61.7 (a Koszul-regular immersion of schemes is perfect)

proof.text: Fix a point y of Y and an affine neighbourhood U=Spec(A) as in the hypothesis, with I=(f_1,\dots,f_r). By the affine description of a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], i^{-1}(U)=Spec(A/I). On an affine open D(g) of U its structure sheaf has sections (A/I)_g, so (i_*\mathcal O_Z)|_U is the sheaf associated to the A-module A/I.

By Koszul-regularity [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence], H_j(K_\bullet(f_1,\dots,f_r))=0 for every j\ne0. The Koszul-complex definition [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex] gives K_0=A, K_1=A^{\oplus r}, and d_1(e_i)=f_i. Hence im(d_1)=(f_1,\dots,f_r)=I and H_0(K_\bullet)=A/I. The quotient map in degree zero and zero maps in other degrees define an augmentation K_\bullet\to A/I; it is a quasi-isomorphism by these homology calculations. Sheafification on Spec(A) is exact, as can be checked after localization at each prime, so this yields a quasi-isomorphism of the sheafified Koszul complex with (i_*\mathcal O_Z)|_U from Step 1.

By [def-weil-pbc-koszul-complex], K_j=\bigwedge^j_A(A^{\oplus r}) is finite free with basis indexed by the j-element subsets of {1,\dots,r}, and K_j=0 for j>r. The augmentation of Step 2 is therefore a finite free resolution of A/I. Its sheafification gives a strictly perfect complex on U representing (i_*\mathcal O_Z)|_U. Since the chosen affine neighbourhoods cover Y, the definition [def-pc-perfect-complex] gives that i_*\mathcal O_Z is a perfect complex on Y.

For every chosen affine U=Spec(A), Step 3 supplies a finite resolution of A/I by finite free A-modules. The local criterion for a perfect closed immersion [def-sc-perfect-closed-immersion] applies to this covering, so i is perfect as a morphism of schemes. For the empty scheme the covering is empty and the conclusion holds vacuously; for r=0 the complex is A in degree zero, while for r=1 it is A\xrightarrow{f_1}A and Koszul-regularity makes the positive homology vanish.
